DIV8.HEAD: § 117.4 Definitions.
DIV8.P: The following definitions apply to this part:
Drawbridge means a bridge with an operational span that is intended to be opened for the passage of waterway traffic.
Drawtender. means the person who operates a drawbridge.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.5 When the drawbridge must open.
DIV8.P: Except as otherwise authorized or required by this part, drawbridges must open promptly and fully for the passage of vessels when a request or signal to open is given in accordance with this subpart.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.31 Drawbridge operations for emergency vehicles and emergency vessels.
DIV8.P: (a) Upon receiving notification that an emergency vehicle is responding to an emergency situation, a drawtender must make all reasonable efforts to have the drawspan closed at the time the emergency vehicle arrives.

(b) When a drawtender receives notice, or a proper signal, the drawtender shall take all reasonable measures to have the draw opened, regardless of the operating schedule of the draw, for passage of the following, provided this opening does not conflict with local emergency management procedures which have been approved by the cognizant Coast Guard Captain of the Port:
(1) Federal, State, and local government vessels used for public safety;
(2) Vessels in distress where a delay would endanger life or property;
(3) Commercial vessels engaged in rescue or emergency salvage operations; and
(4) Vessels seeking shelter from severe weather.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.40 Advance notice for drawbridge opening.
DIV8.P: (a) Upon written request by the owner of a drawbridge, the District Commander may authorize a drawbridge to operate under an advance notice for opening. The drawtender, after receiving the advance notice, shall open the draw at the requested time.
(b) If the request is approved, a description of the advance notice for the drawbridge will be added to subpart B of this part.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.821 Smith River.
DIV8.P: (a) The draw of the Main Street drawbridge, mile 3.4, at Smithfield, need not open from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. and from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday except Federal holidays.
(b) The draw of the Smith River Railroad Bridge, mile 5.1, at Smithfield, shall open on signal if at least four hours notice is given.
(c) The Main Street drawbridge, mile 3.4, is operated by the Smithfield Department of Public Works.
(d) The Main Street drawbridge, mile 3.4, has a vertical clearance of 12 feet above mean high water in the closed position.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.901 Harbor River.
DIV8.P: (a) The draw of the Harbor Avenue Bridge, mile 0.8, at Bristol, shall open on signal.
(b) From November 1 through March 31, the draw of the Harbor Avenue Bridge shall open on signal if at least 24 hours notice is given.
(c) The owner of the Harbor Avenue Bridge shall post the notice requirement of paragraph (b) of this section on signs visible to approaching vessels.

DIV8.HEAD: § 117.1081 Coast Channel.
DIV8.P: (a) The draw of the Coast Channel Bridge, mile 2.2, at Port Angeles, shall operate as follows:
(1) The draw shall open as required by §§ 117.5 and 117.31.
(2) The draw need not open from 6:30 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. Monday through Friday.
(b) Vessels approaching the security zone near the Coast Channel Bridge shall comply with 33 CFR part 165.
(c) The owner of the Coast Channel Bridge shall maintain the clearance gauges required by § 117.999.
